title: GR Photo: the companion app for Ricoh GR cameras
description: Edit, save and load Image Control, download and geotag your photos, and shoot from your phone. Free and open source, on iOS and Android.
heroTitle: The companion app for Ricoh GR cameras
heroText: Edit, save and load Image Control. Download and geotag your photos. Shoot from your phone. Fast, free and open source, on iOS and Android.
fastText: Photos and previews come off the camera quickly, and the Library opens from what is already on your phone.
platformsText: The same app on an iPhone or an Android phone.
openText: MIT License. No account, no ads, no tracking.
languagesText: Every language your GR's menus are in.
editText: Change every parameter and see what it does to your own photo before you shoot with it.
saveText: Save the Image Control a shot was taken with in one tap, and keep your looks on your phone. A couple more taps load one into your camera.
shootText: A shutter button over Bluetooth, or live view over Wi-Fi with focus and exposure.
downloadText: Browse the whole card, save JPEG or RAW, and let your phone add the location to every shot.
endText: For the GR III, GR IIIx and GR IV, including the HDF bodies and the GR IV Monochrome. iOS 15.5 or later, Android 12 or later.
independent: GR Photo is an independent project and is not affiliated with Ricoh.
altLibrary: The Library: the photos on the camera's card by day, with filters for JPEG, RAW and video
altViewerDetails: A photo's details: its format, size, date and Image Control, with Save look
altViewerMap: A photo with a map of where it was taken
altLooks: Looks: the camera's three Custom slots above the looks saved on the phone
altLooksLoad: Loading a saved look into the camera's C2 slot
altLookEditor: The look editor on its Tone tab, with a before and after preview
altLookEditorColour: The look editor on its Colour tab, with a before and after preview
altRemote: Remote: the shutter button, self-timer and drive mode over Bluetooth
altLiveView: Live view: the camera's picture with exposure readouts and the shutter button
